newsitem.title: INDIA: India to hold Miss World show despite attack -- firm.
newsitem.headline: India to hold Miss World show despite attack -- firm.

text.p: India will go ahead with its first Miss World beauty contest, despite suicide threats by a women's group and a failed attack, organisers said on Monday.
Controversy has dogged the contest since Amitabh Bachchan Corporation Ltd, an entertainment firm launched by India's most popular film star, announced it would be held here next month.
Protesters ransacked the former offices of the sponsoring company, target of outrage by traditionalist groups.

"We are going ahead with the show," Manohar Arcot, general manager of the organisers, told Reuters in Bangalore, a day after demonstrators wrecked premises here, not realising the firm had moved a month ago.
Police have beefed up security at the new offices of Amitabh Bachchan Corporation Ltd (ABCL) at the Chinnaswamy cricket ground where Miss World will be crowned on November 23.
Police said Sunday's attack, which caused $5,600 worth of damage, was a mistake by intruders who told staff at the firm's old premises they wanted the show called off.
An anonymous caller later told police that it was a warning to ABCL not to stage the event.
Several organisations, including the militant Farmers' Association, which has a history of attacks against multi-national companies, have protested against the event being held in this southern city.
The group denied responsibility for the attack.

But its leader, M.D. Nanjundaswamy, has called for "direct action" against cinemas showing films starring screen idol Amitabh Bachchan, whose company holds the licence for staging this year's Miss World.
A women's group, the Mahila Jagarna Samiti (Forum to Awaken Women), has threatened to send a suicide squad to commit self-immolation to disrupt the show.

Nearly a week ago the various opposition groups organised a rally at which Ananth Kumar, a Bangalore parliamentarian for the main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), threatened that over 100,000 people will lay siege to the beauty gala.
The groups issued a joint statement denouncing the show as a cultural invasion, and said it represented a commercialisation and exploitation of women by multi-national companies.
